title: Chicken Chasseur
subtitle: Chicken braised in white wine with tomatoes and mushrooms
excerpt: Chicken thighs browned and braised in a sauce of white wine, tomatoes, tarragon, and mushrooms. Poulet chasseur (the hunter's chicken) is one of the great French bistro dishes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Poulet chasseur ('hunter's chicken') is a French bistro classic, the name referring to the garnish of mushrooms and tomatoes characteristic of dishes prepared 'in the hunter's style' (a la chasseur). The dish became popular in British restaurants and homes in the 1960s and 1970s as French cooking became fashionable. Unlike coq au vin, chasseur uses white wine, which gives a lighter, brighter sauce. The tarragon is essential to the flavour: it is the defining herb of French chicken cookery and should not be substituted.

content.text: Brown the chicken skin-side down in batches without moving it: a deep golden crust gives the sauce its body and colour. The wine must reduce by at least half before adding the stock, or the sauce will taste thin and raw. Add the fresh tarragon right at the end, off the heat, so its flavour stays bright rather than cooked out.
Heat the oil in a wide casserole. Season the chicken and brown skin-side down for 6 to 8 minutes until deep golden. Turn and brown the other side. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, soften the shallot for 4 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute. Add the mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes until golden.

Pour in the wine. Simmer briskly for 5 minutes until reduced by half. Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, thyme, and bay leaves. Return the chicken, skin-side up. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook over low heat for 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
Remove the thyme and bay leaves. Check seasoning. Stir in the fresh tarragon off the heat. Serve with mashed potato, rice, or crusty bread.
